# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

+///    (a syntax error) fails with the excerpt.

+/// that ran, and the failure text carries the error excerpt.

+  const AppPreflightOutcome({required this.gate});
+
+  /// Which gate ran: `flutter-test` or `smoke-render`.
+  final String gate;
+}

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

```bash

```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

+

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

```bash

The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG

  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```

- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108

- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

+/// gh-1164 Part C: the pre-flight gate on the app handover path — the
+/// `open_app` tool call NEVER returns success for an app whose JS fails to
+/// load/render or whose test is red (the "no fake success" contract, AC7).
+///
+/// Gate selection (AC10):
+///
+/// 1. **`flutter-test`** — the app's standing test `test/apps/<id>_test.dart`
+///    exists AND the host provides a [FlutterTestRunner] (it can spawn the
+///    toolchain). A red test fails with the failure excerpt.
+/// 2. **`smoke-render`** — everywhere else (sandboxed hosts cannot run
+///    `flutter test`): the app boots headlessly in a real JS engine; the
+///    gate requires a first render with no captured error within the
+///    budget. A load-time throw, a `jsr.showError`, or "no render at all"
+///    (a syntax error) fails with the excerpt.
+///
+/// The gate never degrades to a silent skip: every outcome NAMES the gate
+/// that ran, and the failure text carries the error excerpt.
+///
+/// Web safety: the native-bridge probe ([jsEngineBootable]) lives in a
+/// conditional-import pair (`app_preflight_probe_io.dart` /
+/// `app_preflight_probe_stub.dart`) — dart:ffi has no web target, and on
+/// the web the JS engine ships inside the page bundle anyway (the stub
+/// reports bootable). The gate itself (engine boot + tree read) is pure
+/// Dart and compiles for every surface.

+import 'package:fa/apps/js_app_error_channel.dart';

+export 'package:fa/apps/app_preflight_probe_stub.dart'
+    if (dart.library.io) 'package:fa/apps/app_preflight_probe_io.dart';
+
+/// The outcome of one gate run; [gate] is always named.
+sealed class AppPreflightOutcome {
+  const AppPreflightOutcome({required this.gate});
+
+  /// Which gate ran: `flutter-test` or `smoke-render`.
+  final String gate;
+}
+
+/// The app passed its gate (green test, or a clean first render).
+class AppPreflightPassed extends AppPreflightOutcome {
+  const AppPreflightPassed({required super.gate});
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'pre-flight $gate: passed';
+}
+
+/// The app failed its gate; [excerpt] is the bounded failure text for the
+/// tool result (AC7: the tool result itself is a failure carrying the

+class AppPreflightFailed extends AppPreflightOutcome {
+  const AppPreflightFailed({required super.gate, required this.excerpt});
+
+  final String excerpt;
+

+}

+abstract class FlutterTestRunner {

+  Future<FlutterTestResult> runAppTest(String appId);
+}
+
+/// Result of one [FlutterTestRunner] invocation.
+class FlutterTestResult {
+  const FlutterTestResult({required this.passed, required this.output});

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart

Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]

  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

+/// load/render or whose test is red (the "no fake success" contract, AC7).

+/// Gate selection (AC10):

+///    (a syntax error) fails with the excerpt.
+///
+/// The gate never degrades to a silent skip: every outcome NAMES the gate
+/// that ran, and the failure text carries the error excerpt.

+/// conditional-import pair (`app_preflight_probe_io.dart` /

+  const AppPreflightOutcome({required this.gate});
+
+  /// Which gate ran: `flutter-test` or `smoke-render`.
+  final String gate;
+}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

blocks.text:
Interesting details:

1. `__faFingerprint`: normalizes digits out entirely — this could over-collapse distinct errors (e.g. "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'x.0')" vs "x.1"). But that's the design trade-off mentioned.

2. The bootstrap wraps `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` globally in the JS runtime. Potential issue: `setTimeout = function...` — assigning to undeclared variable in sloppy mode creates global; ok. But if the runtime re-reads originals... fine.

3. `jsr.showError` wrapper: `return baseShowError(msg)` — original may not return anything; ok.

4. Duplicate reporting: a runtime throw in a RAF callback gets reported by the `__wrapCb` as 'callback' AND by window.onerror as 'onerror' (if the bridge routes exceptions to onerror). Then dedup collapses them via fingerprint... but messages may differ between callback and onerror paths. Actually wrapCb catches, so it won't reach onerror. OK.

5. `_forwardError` with `errorSink != null`: forwards raw event without gate. Fine — local collector.

6. `reportHostError`: kind parsing via `JsAppErrorKind.values.asNameMap()[kind]` — allocates each call, minor.

7. In the smoke gate, `_awaitFirstRender` — engine.tree.value is the rendered tree. OK.

8. `computeSourceRevision` hashes `dir`, `entryFile`, and whole tree — but the buffer starts with `$dir/$entryFile\n` and then walks `dir` — the walk includes the entry file too (as part of dir). Fine.

Wait — one issue: `_sourceRevision` computed from `env` (the engine's env), which for live engines is the real env. OK.

9. Note: the engine boot calls `_assembleEntryJs()` then `computeSourceRevision` — both walk the tree. Minor perf, fine.

Now, `_handleEngineLog` forwards every faAppError line. But also — errors captured during smoke probe: `errors.first.event.message` — note the SmokeProbeError.revision unused in excerpts? `SmokeProbeError` stores revision for "the gate summary can name the exact source that failed" but I don't see revision used in any excerpt in runSmokeRenderGate. Let me check... In the failure excerpts, revision is never included. So the `revision` field is captured but never used — dead-ish. Actually wait, let me re-read: errors list is SmokeProbeError; excerpts use `errors.first.event.message` only. So SmokeProbeError.revision is write-only → dead code / SUGGESTION. Hmm, maybe minor. Actually let me grep whether anything reads `.revision` of SmokeProbeError.

Also `capExcerpt(errors.first.event.message)` caps message at 500 but the message field itself was already capped? In JS, message is String(message) — unbounded from JS. Capped at gate. OK.

Also: `_awaitFirstRender` — after engine.start() the tree might already be set; checked. If tree never renders and no errors — fails with "syntax error" hint. Good.

Important: In `runSmokeRenderGate`, if `engine.start()` succeeds but render budget elapses with captured errors present — handled.

But one subtle issue: `errorSink` reports ALL captured errors locally, but the smoke gate checks `errors.isNotEmpty` only AFTER first render. If an app renders first, then throws asynchronously later (after gate passed), gate passes — acceptable (first render clean).

Now the timer wrap: `setTimeout = function(fn, ms) { return baseSetTimeout(__wrapCb(fn), ms); };` — this drops extra arguments beyond ms? `setTimeout(fn, ms, arg1, arg2)` — the wrapper only passes (fn, ms)! Extra args are lost. js_widget_runtime apps may use setTimeout with args (rare in JS, but valid). Also `this` context: baseSetTimeout called as bare function — in JS, calling `baseSetTimeout(...)` without receiver: if baseSetTimeout is an native or bound function, fine. Potential minor. This is injected bootstrap code — a SUGGESTION-level finding: wrapper drops trailing args: `return baseSetTimeout(__wrapCb(fn), ms)` should be `return baseSetTimeout.apply(null, arguments)` with wrapped fn. Worth a suggestion comment.

Also `requestAnimationFrame` wrapper drops the timestamp argument? No — `__wrapCb(fn)` returns function() { return fn.apply(this, arguments); } — inner wrapper forwards its own arguments. Good. Only setTimeout/setInterval lose extra args since the outer wrapper signature is (fn, ms).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 108
- **Additions**: +4231
- **Deletions**: -81
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T01:53:46Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>
